summary: The profile is close. These changes name the tools, the region, and the trigger events the page actually covers.

items.text: Operations and office managers, IT leads, and owner-operators at US and Canadian businesses with 10 to 250 staff. Not developers. They live in Gmail or Outlook.
items.detail: The page says "no developer required" and addresses office staff, so naming non-developers and company size makes prompts more specific.

items.text:
A carrier email-to-text gateway (txt.att.net, vtext.com) stopped delivering their alerts
A monitoring tool such as Datadog or Grafana only sends email alerts
A missed alert caused damage or a missed shift
They hit the 10DLC registration wall
A developer quote for a Twilio build came back too expensive
items.detail: Each one is a named event on the page that sends a buyer looking now.

items.text:
SMS marketers: the page is about alerts to staff, not campaigns
Developers building SMS into a product: they want an API
Teams that need acknowledgement and escalation: PagerDuty or Opsgenie fits them better
items.detail: The page points escalation needs to PagerDuty, so saying so keeps prompts away from the wrong buyers.

items.text:
Setup in about 30 minutes
Nothing new for staff to install
Replies come back to the inbox
Compliance (10DLC) handled for them
About [$29 to $49 a month]
items.detail: The page states the setup time and replies to email. The price is not on this page.
items.verify: Check the current plan prices before using them in a prompt.

caution: The price range in values is in [brackets] because this page does not state it.
